title: Jump Game
statement:
You are given an array `nums` of non-negative integers. You start standing on index `0`. If you are standing on index `i`, you may jump forward to any index from `i + 1` to `i + nums[i]` (inclusive), as long as it stays inside the array. In other words, `nums[i]` is the **maximum** jump length from that position, and a value of `0` means you cannot move from there.

Decide whether you can reach the last index. Print `true` if you can and `false` otherwise. An array with a single element is already at its last index.

In the interview you were also asked to dry-run your loop with the variable values at every step and state the time and space complexity, so be ready to explain why your approach is correct.
inputFormat:
The first line contains `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `nums[0] ... nums[n-1]`.

examples.explanation: Jump 1 step from index 0 to index 1, then 3 steps from index 1 straight to the last index.
From index 0 you can only reach index 1; from there you reach index 2 or 3. Index 3 leads only to index 4, which has value 0, so index 5 is never reached.
Jump to index 1, then 3 steps to index 4 (skipping the zeros), then 2 steps to the last index 6.

hints: A brute-force search over every jump choice is exponential; think about which indices are reachable rather than which paths exist.
If you can reach index `i`, then every index up to `i + nums[i]` is also reachable, so the reachable indices always form a prefix.
Scan left to right keeping the furthest index reachable so far. If the scan arrives at an index beyond that furthest reach, you are stuck.

            a[-1] = rng.randint(0, 4)

    a[N - 2] = 0
